event_identity.event_name: 2023 Indian Ocean/Arabian Sea marine heatwave context
event_identity.hazard_label: Marine heatwave and coastal ecosystem impact

judge_anchors: The priority should be marine heatwave coastal ecosystem heat stress.
The dominant mechanism is persistent anomalously warm sea-surface conditions.
The answer should use the 183-day April-September window and marine heat-stress index concepts.
The score is built only from event identity, marine report/catalog context, and marine heat-stress terms.
The answer should avoid unsupported precise SST anomaly, Degree Heating Week, coral mortality, flood dominance, or basin-wide impact claims.

criteria.description: Selects marine_heatwave_coastal_ecosystem_heat_stress_priority or an equivalent compact label.
criteria.name: Priority label
criteria.partial_credit: 2 points for a marine heatwave label that omits the coastal ecosystem heat-stress priority.

criteria.description: Identifies persistent anomalously warm sea-surface conditions as the controlling mechanism.
criteria.name: Dominant mechanism
criteria.partial_credit: 1.5 points for a generic warm-ocean or heatwave mechanism without persistence or sea-surface emphasis.

criteria.description: Connects marine heatwave conditions to coral bleaching heat stress and coastal ecosystem risk.
criteria.name: Impact pathway
criteria.partial_credit: 1.5 points for naming either coral bleaching heat stress or ecosystem risk.

criteria.description: Reports the 183-day event window and marine_evidence_score 9/9.
criteria.name: Event duration and evidence score
criteria.partial_credit: Partial credit for correct duration or a mostly correct evidence score.

criteria.description: Names at least three marine heat-stress index or product concepts from the local marine context.
criteria.name: Marine index concepts
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1 point per valid term, capped at 3.

criteria.description: Bases the decision on marine event identity and marine report/catalog context rather than land-weather, population, AOI, or terrestrial remote-sensing proxies.
criteria.name: Source-scope discipline
criteria.partial_credit: 1 point if the answer mentions land proxies but keeps them clearly secondary.

criteria.description: Avoids unsupported precise SST anomaly, Degree Heating Week, coral mortality, flooding dominance, or exact basin-wide impact claims.
criteria.name: Overclaim control
criteria.partial_credit: 1 point if only one minor unsupported detail is included.
